analysis:
All changed files in this batch are test-only (ProviderCoreTests). No production source is shown, so no control is observed to be weakened or added here.

NemotronSuperLocalImageBindingTests.swift: the tests now assert that encodedHeaderQuote uses NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes as the ingress ceiling. A body over the maximum fails with the new Failure.bodyTooLarge, and zero or oversized-template input fails with invalidInput. The quote formula (body*32 + template*4 + 16 MiB) is asserted. Remote URLs, file:// URIs, non-base64 data URIs, gif and jpg labels, and logprobs are still rejected as unsupportedCapability. Busy/cancel/closed tests check that reservations are refunded to baseline, which supports the A-001 and availability posture. The large base64 blob is the pinned NVIDIA chat template fixture, which is test data.

NemotronSuperOpenRouterVideoTests.swift (new): it reads committed SDK video resources, checks their SHA-256, and drives parse, inspect, prompt, plan and decode, then serving on the fixture. It asserts that ingress plus plan bytes stay within Policy.videoMediaChargeBytes and that charges return to baseline. The file path comes from #filePath, a test-only value that does not touch a runtime trust boundary.

NemotronSuperVideoBindingTests.swift: the video charge expectation rises from 3,751,221,756 to 4,875,295,228 bytes, which fits the larger ingress bound. A new test checks that bodyTooLarge maps to mediaTooLarge and invalidInput to invalidMedia. The helper visibility change (VideoOwner, videoOwner and SuperVideoEvents made internal) is confined to the test target.

Integration questions for production-side review (not visible here): (1) the raised maximumEncodedBodyBytes and the larger video charge, namely whether they stay bounded by GlobalKVCacheBudget and cannot be abused for DoS by a malicious consumer or coordinator path (T-010, T-029); (2) whether the media_too_large code is sanitized and leaks nothing; (3) the test comment says 413 at the coordinator while the unit asserts statusCode 400 in the provider, so the coordinator's mapping needs confirming. The decoded plaintext media handling should be checked against T-050 for no temp files, but that code is unchanged and not shown.
